definition: The coordinating service at the center of the book's design: it keeps durable records and checks each change it governs before that change takes effect.
The person who runs a machine and answers for the agents working on it.
A program, usually built around a language model, that observes its task and proposes actions such as edits, test runs or payments.
The governed environment agents work in: a daemon holds the shared record and decides, for each change an agent proposes, whether that change takes effect.
A background service; in this book, the trusted program that holds a harbor's shared record and performs the admission check.
The single check in the write path that decides whether a proposed change takes effect; to admit a change means only to let it pass this check and happen.
The daemon's authoritative account of who holds which resources, who owes what and what has been paid.
A recorded permission stating what its holder may do, to which resources and until when.
A grant signed by the daemon, which the daemon checks before it admits a change the holder proposes.
